cur:monumental-san-venanzio-apse-christ.summary: In the clouds at the top of the apse, a bust of Christ with long dark hair and beard raises his hand in blessing, flanked by two angels who emerge from the streaked red and blue sky. Below him (not shown here) stands the Virgin in prayer among apostles and Dalmatian martyrs whose relics were brought to Rome.
facts: Pope John IV (640–642), a native of Dalmatia, brought relics of Dalmatian saints to Rome and built an oratory in their honour, decorated with mosaics that include his own portrait holding a model of the building.

cur:monumental-san-venanzio-apse-christ.notes: Commons file names call the chapel 'cappella di s. teodoro' and date the mosaic 'c. 650'; the usual name is the Chapel of San Venanzio.
